title: Microsoft is cutting eight Copilot shortcuts from Windows 11, including the useful one
excerpt: Microsoft's cleanup removes eight OneDrive Copilot entries from File Explorer and eliminates the image compare tool.
content_html:
Published Oct 21, 2026, 7:12 AM EDT

Sara Heritage is a tech and gaming journalist, who's currently making her way up to Master Ball rank in Pokemon Champions. Bylines in IGN, GAMINGbible, The Gamer and more. You can usually find her tinkering with tech, or restoring old consoles, always with one of her 3 cats nearby. Come and talk with her over on Twitter @SHeritageJourno.

Summary

  • Microsoft is removing eight OneDrive Copilot actions from File Explorer’s right‑click menu.
  • Removal includes the useful AI Compare Images shortcut; now you must chat with Copilot or use other tools.
  • Staged removal begins mid-Nov and completes by Dec 2026; use fc in Command Prompt to compare files.

Microsoft is withdrawing several of its AI features from Windows 11 after users voiced their displeasure. The company is removing eight Copilot actions from the new File Explorer right-click menu, calling it a simple cleanup.

Microsoft said, "We are discontinuing the OneDrive Copilot Summarize, Create FAQ, Compare Files, Ask a question, Explain images, Compare images, Extract text actions from the File Explorer context menu as part of this change", according to Windows Insider.

This means Copilot actions will be removed from the File Explorer context menu, if you even had access it yet. Getting rid of the clutter is nice, but there’s a catch. Microsoft is also ditching the one truly useful thing in that menu: the AI-powered Compare Images tool.

Why has Microsoft removed Compare Images from Windows 11?

There’s still a solution to compare your files, but it’s not as easy

New documents in the Microsoft Admin Center claim that these eight OneDrive shortcuts will be discontinued beginning in mid-November 2026 and will be fully removed by December. Once the deadline passes, you won't be able to access summaries, FAQs, text extraction, image explanations, or, most annoyingly of all, file comparisons when you right-click.

Even if you don't like the forced Copilot AI features, I must say that I personally found the Compare Images shortcut pretty useful. Rather than using the general 'Ask Copilot' button or browsing around in the OneDrive activity center, you now have to chat with Copilot and spell out your request.

This isn’t the first time Microsoft has backtracked. In the past year, they’ve renamed or dropped Copilot from Notepad, yanked the Copilot button from Photos, and paused taskbar integrations after users complained.

If you want to compare text files on Windows without relying on File Explorer’s built-in tools or third-party software, you can use the native Command Prompt utility known as fc (File Compare). To use it, open the Start menu, enter cmd and then launch the Command Prompt. Use cd to change to the directory containing the files, then run fc file1.txt file2.txt. The program then examines the files line by line and displays any differences directly in the terminal window.

If you currently use the right-click menu to quickly see the differences between documents, you should start to change over your ways over the next few weeks. After the staged update has been installed on your machine, that useful shortcut will be permanently removed.
